Taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{x-1} & <{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2-x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x-1}) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡[{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2-x}] \\ (x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & <(2-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2}) \\ (x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & <(2-x)(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\ (x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & <(2-x)(0-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\ (x-1)\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & <(x-2)\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡5 & <x\operatorname{ln}⁡2-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡5-x\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & <\operatorname{ln}⁡5-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & <\operatorname{ln}⁡5-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x & <\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5-2\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\end{aligned}
$$
